From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French conservatoire. Doublet of conservatory.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (US) IPA(key): /kənˈsɝvətwɑr/

Noun

[edit]

conservatoire (plural conservatoires)

  1. (music) A music academy.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • college of music
  • conservatory
  • conservatory of music
  • musical school
  • music conservatory
  • music school
  • school of music

Translations

[edit]
school or educational institution that teaches music

  • Belarusian: кансерваторыя f (kansjervatóryja)
  • Bulgarian: консервато́рия f (konservatórija)
  • Chinese:
    Mandarin: 音樂學校 / 音乐学校 (yīnyuè xuéxiào)
  • Dutch: conservatorium (nl) n
  • Finnish: konservatorio (fi)
  • French: conservatoire (fr) m, école de musique (fr) f, école supérieure de musique f, académie de musique f (Belgium)
  • German: Konservatorium (de) n, Musikkonservatorium n, Musikakademie f, Hochschule für Musik f, Musikschule (de) f, höhere Musikschule f, Musikhochschule (de) f
  • Ido: konservatorio (io)
  • Italian: conservatorio (it) m
  • Japanese: コンサーヴァトーリ (konsāvatōri)
  • Kazakh: консерватория (konservatoriä)
  • Kyrgyz: консерватория (ky) (konservatoriya)

  • Russian: консервато́рия (ru) f (konservatórija)

Anagrams

[edit]

French

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kɔ̃.sɛʁ.va.twaʁ/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

From conserver +‎ -(at)oire (adjective-forming suffix), a learned formation built on the supine stem cōnservāt- of Latin cōnservāre, like the noun conservation. Corresponds to the Medieval Latin adjective cōnservātōrius.

Adjective

[edit]

conservatoire (plural conservatoires)

  1. conservative
    Synonym: conservateur
Derived terms
[edit]
  • conservatoirement

Etymology 2

[edit]

From conserver +‎ -(at)oire (masculine-noun-forming suffix), a learned formation built on the supine stem cōnservāt- of Latin cōnservāre. Corresponds to the post-Classical Latin neuter noun of place cōnservātōrium.

Noun

[edit]

conservatoire m (plural conservatoires)

  1. conservatory (for the maintenance of tradition)
  2. music academy
Descendants
[edit]
  • → English: conservatoire
  • → Turkish: konservatuvar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “conservatoire”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
